newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia says Asia foreign policy priority.
newsitem.headline: Australia says Asia foreign policy priority.

text.p: Australia on Wednesday declared closer ties with Asia its top foreign policy priority, as a heated race debate threatened to tarnish the country's regional reputation.
"Australia's engagement with the region is no passing phase," said Foreign Minister Alexander Downer in a speech flagged as a major foreign policy announcement.
"It is the single overriding foreign policy objective of our government. Australia is with Asia for the long-term," Downer told the Australia-Asia Institute in Sydney.
Australia became embroiled in a divisive race debate last month when independent politician Pauline Hanson said Australia was being swamped by Asians and called for an immediate end to immigration.
Asian media has since questioned Australia's commitment to the region, criticising Prime Minister John Howard for not ending the xenophobic debate.
But Asian politicans have said regional governments realise the race comments are not government policy.
Asians make up about 4.7 percent of Australia's 18 million population and about one third of the nation's 100,000 immigrants each year.

Downer said on Wednesday that Australian and Asian security and economic interests were irrevocably bound together. "The reason why we seek closer engagement is...because of the profound benefit which flows from our friendship with the countries of the region and the realisation of our mutual interests," Downer said.
Downer, describing the economic dynamism of Australia's Asian neighbours as an "inevitable force", said Australia recognised the rapid political and economic transformation in the region.
"Put simply, Asia is on the move and it is moving forward at a pace and with a force unparalleled in recent history," he said.
Australia's two-way trade with East Asia in 1995/96 totalled A$73 billion (US$57 billion), with Australia running a heavy surplus of A$17 billion.
